title: The push-skip reader refuses proof from a job that ended success with every step skipped, unless scope says no
why: Source: lane child-ci-q-max, round 1 on q_max #1172 (its read, push-skip.py:137, relayed by the coordinator 04:32 CST Nov 14; neither the coordinator nor triage read it; q_max is outside triage's GitHub scope): a records-only claim commit on a batch branch runs lint only (tests and specimen steps skipped, jobs `success`), so the claim head counts as proof and a push to main skips npm test on a tree whose last full run was the head before the claim. q_max CLAUDE.md:127 ("Main runs the full npm test after each merge") is then false for a proven push. Likely the same in claude-settings for any job skipped at step or job level: read first how #3398's macOS gate (job-level skips) interacts: scope-skipped is intended, an unrun test job is not. The change tightens, it does not widen: the reader refuses proof from a head whose test jobs did not run their steps, unless scope says no. A guard or check change: review round 3 and the net-value test apply. Related by name only, unread: push-skip-proven-tree, push-skip-text-says-stable, macos-jobs-gated-by-scope. Coordinator's interim ruling for q_max #1172: (a) accept claim runs as a named risk in q_max after the lane measures the last 5 claim commits; q_max, not claude-settings, changes its text. The lane also notes q_max decisions one-required-check, only-a-batch-runs-ci and ci-spend-gate carry a "push runs every job" exception to update (q_max's own records). Note 04:40 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 04:40): #3398 changes what push-skip proves for a scope-skipped macOS job; this step reads #3398 after it lands, before it builds.
